verdict.rationale: Gecko documents a v1 API with a published OpenAPI spec. It covers triggering scans, reading scan, repository and vulnerability data, triaging findings, managing schedules, rotating the GitLab token and receiving webhooks, and an MCP server exposes similar actions to AI tools. However, several UI capabilities have no documented API equivalent, so parity is unproven. Missing for 10: API coverage of Request fix / fix-PR creation, repository wiki and endpoint map access, PR-check configuration (fail-on severity), repo/provider connection and ZIP upload, team and API-key management, and an explicit statement or independent verification of full UI parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Gecko's v1 API lets you trigger scans, read scan, repository, and vulnerability data, triage findings, manage scan schedules, rotate your GitLab token, and receive webhook events
Connect it to an AI tool and the tool can list your repositories and scans, pull full vulnerability evidence (proof of concept, call chain, patch diff), triage findings, and file tickets.
PROBE openapi: HTTP 200 at https://gecko.security/openapi.json — contains "openapi" key
PATCH /integrations/gitlab swaps in a fresh token, built for secret managers and rotation scripts.
